fields.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
fields.bodyHtml:
Rheumatoid arthritis: innovative treatment in Israel

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting primarily the small joints of the hands and feet. A distinguishing feature of RA is that it affects the joints symmetrically, which can lead to their deformity and destruction. In Israel, patients with rheumatoid arthritis are offered advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at reducing symptoms as far as possible and preventing the disease from progressing.

Diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis

  1. Laboratory tests
    These include measurement of rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies (anti-CCP), and a full blood count to identify inflammation.
  2. MRI and ultrasound of the joints
    Used to assess the extent of damage to the joints and the presence of inflammation and erosions.
  3. X-rays
    Allow the characteristic changes in the joints associated with RA to be identified, including erosions and osteoporosis around the joints.

Treatments for rheumatoid arthritis in Israel

  1. Drug treatment
    • Disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs): methotrexate, leflunomide and others, used to slow the progression of the disease.
    • Biological medicines: TNF-alpha inhibitors, interleukin inhibitors and other biological agents aimed at controlling the inflammatory process.
    • Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors: The newest class of medicines for treating RA. They act on the inflammatory signalling pathways inside the cells.
  2. Physiotherapy and rehabilitation
    These include a set of exercises aimed at maintaining mobility in the joints, strengthening the muscles and improving general wellbeing.
  3. Surgery
    Used where conservative treatment brings no relief. Surgical options include synovectomy (removal of the inflamed lining of the joint), osteotomy and joint replacement.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Provides a comprehensive view of the problem and the development of an individual treatment plan covering both medicines and physiotherapy.
  • Access to innovative medicines
    Patients are able to receive the most modern medicines, including the latest generation of biological treatments.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israel is home to some of the world's leading rheumatologists, with extensive experience in treating rheumatoid arthritis.
  • Individualised rehabilitation
    Rehabilitation programmes are adapted to the needs of each patient, which aids faster recovery and a better quality of life.

Treatment of rheumatoid arthritis in Israel offers patients not only relief from symptoms and a slowing of the disease, but also the chance to lead an active life with a good quality of life.

fields.title: Type 1 diabetes
fields.bodyHtml:
Type 1 diabetes: advanced approaches to treatment in Israel

Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition in which the immune system attacks the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. Israel offers a comprehensive approach to the diagnosis and treatment of this condition, using modern technology and methods.

Diagnosis of type 1 diabetes in Israel:

  1. Blood glucose measurement
    The main method of establishing a raised level of sugar in the blood.
  2. Glycated haemoglobin test (HbA1c)
    Shows the average level of glucose in the blood.
  3. Autoantibody tests
    Help confirm the autoimmune nature of the condition.
  4. C-peptide measurement
    Helps assess the body's own production of insulin.
  5. Use of a continuous glucose monitor (CGM)
    Allows glucose levels to be tracked continuously, giving more precise control of the condition.
  6. Consultation with a nutritionist
    Development of an individual eating plan adapted to the needs of a patient with type 1 diabetes, which is an important part of the comprehensive approach to treatment.

Treatment of type 1 diabetes in Israel:

  1. Insulin therapy
    The basis of treatment for type 1 diabetes; it involves finding an individual insulin regimen.
  2. Educational programmes
    Teaching patients how to monitor their own blood glucose, eat properly and manage insulin doses.
  3. The use of technology
    Insulin pumps and CGM systems to optimise control of blood glucose levels.
  4. Support and advice
    Psychological support for patients and their families, and access to specialist support groups.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach: Every patient is given an individual treatment and monitoring programme that takes account of their particular needs and way of life.
  • Innovative technology and treatments: Patients have access to the latest advances in the treatment of diabetes, which gives better control of the condition and improves quality of life.
  • A multidisciplinary team of specialists: Doctors, nutritionists, dietitians and psychologists work together to provide a comprehensive approach to treatment and support for patients.

Treatment of type 1 diabetes in Israel aims to achieve and maintain a stable level of glucose in the blood, prevent complications and ensure a good quality of life for patients.

fields.title: Type 2 diabetes
fields.bodyHtml:
Type 2 diabetes: innovative treatment in Israel

Type 2 diabetes is a chronic condition involving a disturbance of glucose metabolism, in which the body's cells lose their sensitivity to insulin. It is the most common type of diabetes and is often linked to excess weight, lifestyle and genetic factors. Israel offers a comprehensive approach to the treatment and control of type 2 diabetes, including advanced methods of diagnosis, individualised treatment and an extensive rehabilitation programme.

Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes:

  1. Blood glucose measurement
    Measurement of blood sugar when fasting and after eating.
  2. Glycated haemoglobin test (HbA1c)
    Allows the average glucose level to be assessed.
  3. Glucose tolerance test (OGTT)
    Helps assess how the body absorbs glucose.
  4. Measurement of C-peptide and insulin
    To assess the production of insulin by the pancreas.
  5. Autoantibody tests
    To rule out the autoimmune causes characteristic of type 1 diabetes.

Treatment of type 2 diabetes in Israel:

  1. Drug therapy
    Includes medicines that improve the sensitivity of cells to insulin, stimulate the production of insulin and lower the level of glucose in the blood.
  2. Lifestyle changes
    Adjusting the diet, increasing physical activity, controlling weight, giving up smoking and limiting alcohol.
  3. Educational programmes
    Teaching patients the basics of managing diabetes, eating properly and monitoring their own blood glucose.
  4. Insulin therapy
    May be prescribed in the later stages of the condition, where medicines and lifestyle changes do not give adequate control of glucose.
  5. Monitoring and control of complications
    Regular monitoring of the cardiovascular system, kidneys, eyes and feet for the prompt detection and treatment of complications.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individualised approach
    Every patient is offered a personal treatment programme that takes account of every aspect of their health and the particular course of their condition.
  • A multidisciplinary team
    Specialists from various fields of medicine work together to provide a comprehensive approach to the treatment and rehabilitation of patients.
  • Access to innovation
    Patients can gain access to the latest medical developments and technology in the treatment of diabetes.
  • Support and education
    Wide opportunities to learn how to manage diabetes, including programmes covering diet, exercise and psychological support.

Treatment of type 2 diabetes in Israel aims to achieve and maintain the target level of glucose in the blood, prevent the development of complications and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Angina
fields.bodyHtml:
Angina: advanced diagnosis and treatment in Israel

Diagnosis of angina:

  1. Clinical examination and history: Analysis of the symptoms and identification of risk factors.
  2. Electrocardiogram (ECG): Assessment of the electrical activity of the heart.
  3. Echocardiography: Imaging of the structure and function of the heart.
  4. Thallium isotope scan of the heart: Assessment of the blood supply to the heart muscle and identification of areas with reduced blood flow.
  5. Cardiac exercise testing: Examination of the working of the heart under exertion on an exercise bike or treadmill.
  6. Laboratory tests: Blood tests, including the lipid profile and markers of inflammation.

Treatments for angina:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Nitrates, beta blockers and calcium channel blockers to control symptoms and improve the blood supply to the heart.
    • Antithrombotic medicines to prevent the formation of clots.
  2. Balloon angioplasty:
    • A minimally invasive procedure in which a balloon is introduced through a catheter to widen the narrowed section of the artery and restore normal blood flow.
  3. Stenting:
    • Placing a stent in the narrowed section of the vessel after balloon angioplasty to keep it open.
  4. Coronary artery bypass grafting:
    • An operation to create a bypass around the narrowed sections of the coronary arteries in order to improve the blood supply to the heart muscle.
  5. A comprehensive rehabilitation programme:
    • Includes physical exercise, dietary advice and teaching on managing stress.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Cardiologists, cardiac surgeons and rehabilitation specialists work together to provide all-round care.
  • Innovative treatments: Access to the most advanced techniques and technology in cardiology.
  • An individual treatment plan: The treatment strategy is chosen according to the particular features of each patient's condition.
  • A high quality of medical care: The use of the newest diagnostic and treatment equipment to achieve the best results.

In Israel, patients with angina receive comprehensive treatment aimed at minimising the risk of cardiovascular events and improving their quality of life.
